title: Enforce one shell, exec or subsystem per SSH session
description:
A preexisting protocol/lifecycle issue was confirmed using raw SSH requests: two exec requests on the same session channel both return accepted=true and can start competing programs sharing stdin, output, exit-status and channel teardown. RFC 4254 permits only one successful shell, exec or subsystem request per session.

xssh/session.go owns PTY/task lifetime but lacks program admission state. Exec dispatch is in xssh/session_handler.go (around line 217), while subsystem dispatch is separately handled in xssh/conn.go (around line 417).

Introduce session-owned admission transitions covering configuration, one accepted program/subsystem, and closing. Reserve running state before spawning work. Apply consistently across shell, exec, SFTP and custom subsystem dispatch, and specify behavior for failed starts and late env/PTY requests so mutable launch settings cannot race startup.

Add raw-protocol regression tests for duplicate and mixed shell/exec/subsystem requests, failure replies, one process owner, cleanup and race-free late configuration. Keep the implementation within xssh, using cohesive types/files before introducing packages.
